cars.specification_market: Original Alfonso XIII / 15T production-road family, selected 1912 long-chassis Torpedo Sport, Revs Institute serial 1858. All seven attributes use that exact museum record. Keep its quoted 3619 cc, 40-45 HP, 118-inch wheelbase and 1764-lb weight without assuming a power test standard, rpm or mass basis. Its CAV lighting and instrument dashboard are documented 1920s modifications, not original 1912 standard equipment. The separate Revs two-seater serial 2110 has different specifications: do not transfer its 3620 cc, 64 hp at 2300 rpm, 104-inch wheelbase, 2215-lb weight or two-seat layout. Manufacturer history quotes 45 CV for the model, not an equation between CV and this museum HP label. Group bodies, chassis, years and road racing appearances once; dedicated racers and replicas are not admitted. Spanish marque origin does not imply Spanish manufacture of the selected French-built example.
cars.summary: The Alfonso XIII helped establish the production sports car: a customer-road family developed from Hispano-Suiza competition engineering. Its significance lies in that transition and its enduring place in early performance-car history. Count the original Alfonso XIII / 15T family once across bodies and years; royal association and rarity alone are not admission reasons.
